# sngl:json on every target: a declared type read from text and written back,
# its marks naming fields and members on the wire, and the failures, worded
# alike everywhere, that say where text did not match.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '5 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '5 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '5 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '5 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '5 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '5 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
// sngl:json reads text as a declared type and writes a value back: a field
// named on the wire by its mark, an option a key that may be missing or null,
// an enum by its member's name, dates as RFC 3339 text, a map of any keys, a
// type that holds itself -- and a failure naming where the text did not match.

import async "sngl:async"
import json "sngl:json"
import time "sngl:time"
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

enum Kind {
    #[json.identifier("hard-cover")]
    hardcover
    paperback
}

struct Score {
    #[json.identifier("base_score")]
    baseScore int
    name      string
}

struct Book {
    id       int
    name     string
    #[json.identifier("page_count")]
    pages    option[int]
    kind     Kind
    scores   list[Score]
    weight   float
    tags     map[string, float]
    finished option[time.date]
    added    time.datetime
}

struct Tree {
    label    string
    children list[Tree]
}

const sample = `{"id": 1, "name": "dune", "kind": "hard-cover", "extra": [1, 2],
    "scores": [{"base_score": 45, "name": "plot"}, {"base_score": 49, "name": "pace"}],
    "weight": 6.9, "tags": {"b": 2, "a": 0.5}, "finished": null, "added": "2024-03-01T12:00:00Z"}`

func failure[T any](r async.Result[T]) => match var f = r {
    ok => ""
    failed => "{f.kind}: {f.message}"
}

func testDecode(t Test) {
    match var b = json.decode[Book](sample) {
        ok {
            t.assert(b.id == 1)
            t.assert(b.name == "dune")
            t.assert(b.pages == null)
            t.assert(b.kind == Kind.hardcover)
            t.assert(b.scores.length() == 2)
            t.assert(b.scores[1].baseScore == 49)
            t.assert(b.weight == 6.9)
            t.assert(b.tags.get("a", 0.0) == 0.5)
            t.assert(b.finished == null)
        }
        failed { t.assert(b.message == "") }
    }
}

// Built in program code, where a date written as text is parsed.
func messiah() Book {
    return Book{
        id = 7,
        name = "dune \"messiah\"",
        pages = 63,
        kind = Kind.paperback,
        scores = [Score{baseScore=44, name="plot"}],
        weight = 9.0,
        tags = {"z" = 1.5, "a" = 2.0},
        finished = time.date("2024-03-01"),
        added = "2024-03-01T12:00:00Z",
    }
}

func testEncode(t Test) {
    var b = messiah()
    t.assert(json.encode(b) == `{"id":7,"name":"dune \"messiah\"","page_count":63,"kind":"paperback","scores":[{"base_score":44,"name":"plot"}],"weight":9,"tags":{"a":2,"z":1.5},"finished":"2024-03-01","added":"2024-03-01T12:00:00Z"}`)
    t.assert(json.encode([1.5, 0.25, 100.0]) == "[1.5,0.25,100]")
    t.assert(json.encode("tab\tline\n") == `"tab\tline\n"`)
}

func testRoundTrip(t Test) {
    var tree = Tree{label="root", children=[Tree{label="a", children=[]}, Tree{label="b", children=[Tree{label="c", children=[]}]}]}
    var out = json.encode(tree)
    t.assert(out == `{"label":"root","children":[{"label":"a","children":[]},{"label":"b","children":[{"label":"c","children":[]}]}]}`)
    match var back = json.decode[Tree](out) {
        ok {
            t.assert(back.children[1].children[0].label == "c")
            t.assert(json.encode(back) == out)
        }
        failed { t.assert(back.message == "") }
    }
}

func testFailures(t Test) {
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[Book](`{"id": 1.5}`)) == "decode: $.id: want an integer")
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[Book](`{"id": 1}`)) == "decode: $.name: missing")
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[list[Score]](`[{"base_score": 1, "name": 2}]`)) == "decode: $[0].name: want a string")
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[Kind](`"ebook"`)) == "decode: $: want one of hard-cover, paperback")
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[int](`[1`)) == "decode: not JSON")
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[map[string, int]](`{"b": 1, "a": "x"}`)) == "decode: $.a: want an integer")
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[time.date](`"2024-02-30"`)) == "decode: $: want a date")
    t.assert(failure(json.decode[option[int]](`null`)) == "")
}

component panel node {
    var shown = "-"
    text #result(value=shown)
    button #run(text="Decode", @click {
        match var s = json.decode[Score](`{"base_score": 3, "name": "style"}`) {
            ok { shown = "{s.name} {s.baseScore}" }
            failed { shown = s.message }
        }
    })
}

func testInAHandler(t Test, c panel) {
    c.run.click()
    t.assert(c.result.value == "style 3")
}

window {
    panel
}
